bug_semantics: In CamaleonCMS UsersController (admin), the authorization filter and the action body resolve the target user from DIFFERENT request parameters: validate_role reads `user_id_param` = `params[:id] || params[:user_id]` (preferring the query-string :id) while updated_ajax loads the account with `current_site.users.find(params[:user_id])` (the path segment). An authenticated low-privileged user sends PATCH /admin/users/<victim_id>/updated_ajax?id=<own_id>: the self-authorization check passes because user_id_param equals the caller's own id, but the action mutates the victim — including overwriting the administrator's password via the password branch — yielding full site takeover through IDOR/parameter confusion (CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key).
flaw_origin: Commit bbdf01c2bf9bb12e8c51203b3cbc430b3180a3eb ("Fixed user authentication when editing profile", 2016-06-24, author+committer RafaelCostella <rafael.costella@usp.br>) created the parameter-confusion design: it introduced the `user_id_param` helper returning `params[:id] || params[:user_id]` and rewired validate_role to compare `cama_current_user.id.to_s == user_id_param` — but updated_ajax continued to load the target with `params[:user_id]` (the split existed as early as the 2015 controller move 415cbda60318, where validate_role checked params[:id] while updated_ajax used params[:user_id]; bbdf01c2 cemented the split by naming and preferring it). From that commit the self-check and the mutated record can diverge. Parent 5e42c93cb has the pre-helper form; the confusion itself (check on :id, act on :user_id) is introduced by bbdf01c2's helper with :id preferred.
